title: trainproof: a deterministic linter for ML training runs
description:
trainproof is a deterministic linter for machine-learning training runs. It issues PASS / WARN / NOT-CHECKED / FAIL verdicts across a run's whole life: an environment and dataset preflight before a single GPU-second is spent, a live guardian during training that can abort a doomed run, a post-run autopsy, and a comparison against a known-good baseline.

No ML judging ML. Every verdict is a rule that either fires or does not, every finding cites the exact numbers behind it, and a check that could not run is reported as NOT-CHECKED rather than as a pass. There are no invented confidence scores.

It reads five log formats, including TensorBoard event files decoded directly from the wire format with no TensorFlow, TensorBoard, protobuf, torch or numpy installed, validated byte-exact against TensorBoard's own EventAccumulator.

From v0.18.0 it also reads the training objective rather than only the run: TP-OBJ-IGNORE-INDEX-COLLISION detects a cross-entropy ignore_index that is also a valid class in the output layer, a collision that silently discards every target carrying that id before the loss is computed, and TP-OBJ-DEAD-CLASS detects a class the model can emit that never once appears as a training target. Both are decidable at step 0 and are deliberately independent of the loss curve: in a controlled reproduction, the broken and corrected runs end at 0.0035 and 0.0034 final loss, indistinguishable by any curve-shaped diagnostic, while the broken model never learns to terminate.

The rules are grounded in an 18-run fault-injection study (Qwen2.5-3B QLoRA, RTX 5080; six configurations at three seeds each) with every real log shipped in-repo, plus real fine-tunes from three frameworks: HuggingFace, Coqui XTTS and PyTorch Lightning.
